subject: MSA addendum & VPC evidence orchestration / legal touchpoints
messages:
From: Julie Klein <julie.klein@medsystech.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA addendum — VPC evidence & operator access

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Procurement and legal at MedSys need a concise path to close the MSA addendum and the Order Form. Two asks from our side: 

1) A clear evidence matrix that shows what operator access / snapshots you will provide (and under what conditions). We need to present this to our InfoSec panel on Monday.
2) A statement on whether witness-style on-prem snapshots are required, or if a validated snapshot deposit + KMS attestation will suffice for our auditors.

Can you send an internal contact for legal redlines and an approximate timeline for delivering a redline-friendly MSA addendum? We prefer to avoid an on-site witness if at all possible, but will consider if the auditors insist.

Attaching the procurement checklist for reference.

Julie
Senior Sourcing Manager
MedSys Tech

Attachments: procurement_checklist_medsys.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Klein <julie.klein@medsystech.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA addendum — VPC evidence & operator access

Hi Julie —

Appreciate the clarity. High level reply below and looping in legal/ops:

- Evidence matrix: We have a draft matrix that maps snapshot types (forensic snapshot, nightly backup, runtime KV export), delivery mechanism (S3 deposit with signed manifest, on-demand console export, secure courier for physical media), and what auditors can validate (hashes, time-stamped manifests, witness attestation). I attached the working matrix (evidence_matrix_medtech.xlsx).
- Witness vs deposit: For most customers we provide a witnessless deposit flow: a sealed snapshot deposited to your S3 under a mutually agreed retention policy plus KMS-derived attestation (HSM signature from our side). That usually satisfies auditors. Where customers insist, we can coordinate a limited witness event (onsite or videowitness).

Next steps from our side: David and Marissa will draft a concise MSA addendum (scope + acceptance criteria + operator access carveouts) and provide redlines by EOD Monday. Lauren will coordinate SOW/order form finalizations. If MedSys needs a witness, please flag immediately so we can calendar necessary ops resources.

Hannah
Director, Customer & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_matrix_medtech.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Klein <julie.klein@medsystech.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA addendum — VPC evidence & operator access

Julie / Hannah,

Thanks — quick legal note on approach. We'll aim to keep the addendum tight: license scope for private deployment, operator activities (maintenance, emergency debug), evidence delivery commitments, and a narrow audit window for custody verification. A few items we plan to propose: 

- Define "snapshot" and "forensic snapshot" precisely (hashing/manifest requirements).
- Evidence delivery: deposit to customer-controlled bucket + signed manifest from Redwood's KMS/HSM. We will include retention / deletion lifecycle in the addendum and an SLA for access requests.
- Operator access: emergency console access must be scoped (time-limited, logged, and pre-authorized via POA). No persistent operator SSH/RDP.
- Witness alternative: include an "Escrow-lite" clause that permits either (a) sealed deposit + third-party attestation or (b) a supervised witness event — customer to choose at request time, with cost / scheduling responsibilities clarified.

Open questions for MedSys (Julie):
1) Do you require custody transfer certification from a specific third-party auditor or is an internal compliance signoff sufficient?
2) Any jurisdictional constraints on data residency we should call out in the addendum?

I'll attach our first-pass redline of the addendum and a simple order-form SOW that enumerates the snapshot cadence and retention. Link to redlines below.

-David
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MSA_Addendum_MedSys_v0.1_redlines.docx (docx); OrderForm_SOW_MedSys_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Julie Klein <julie.klein@medsystech.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, legal@medsystech.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA addendum — VPC evidence & operator access

David — thank you. Answers below inline.

1) Custody transfer certification: MedSys prefers third-party attestation where feasible; our compliance team will accept a neutral SOC2 Type II auditor or an independent forensics firm with chain-of-custody experience. If Redwood can provide the KMS/HSM attestation + a supporting third-party attestation that should be fine.
2) Data residency: production PHI data must remain in US regions only; that should be enforced in the Order Form and mirrored in the addendum.

Regarding the Escrow-lite option: procurement will levy cost-sharing for witness events. Can you recommend a default fallback (we prefer deposit + attestation if it reduces cost and scheduling friction).

Julie

On a separate note, compliance wants an approximate timeline to close legal redlines so we can schedule our audit panel. Would EOD Monday be realistic for Redwood's team to deliver a redline-ready draft?

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: Julie Klein <julie.klein@medsystech.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA addendum — VPC evidence & operator access

Julie —

We can deliver the redline-ready addendum and updated order form by EOD Monday (2026-11-22) as requested. Plan and responsibilities below: 

- Legal (David): final redlines + concise commentary on custody/attestation language (deliverable: MSA_Addendum_MedSys_v0.2_redlines.docx).
- Product/Ops (Marissa): finalize evidence matrix with concrete deposit steps and S3 bucket naming pattern so your auditors can verify manifests.
- Sales/PO (Lauren): finalize order form SOW with PHI-in-US residency enforcement and pricing for optional witness events.
- Compliance outreach (Grace): I'll introduce Grace to MedSys compliance (if ok) to align on acceptable third-party attestors and the audit checklist.

If MedSys accepts deposit + KMS/HSM attestation as the default, we'll include Escrow-lite as a fallback with defined cost split and a 60-day scheduling window. If you prefer an immediate clause allowing MedSys to require a witness, we can add trigger conditions (e.g., classification of data as high-risk) but that typically extends timelines.

I'll share the deliverables via the Drive link and ping the DocuSign placeholder once the SOW is final.

Thanks — talk Monday morning if you want a quick alignment call before your audit panel.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer & Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

Related links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example-docs
Attachments: MSA_Addendum_MedSys_v0.2_redlines.docx; OrderForm_SOW_MedSys_v4.pdf; evidence_matrix_medtech.xlsx
